reviews.comment: I truly believe this man gets some sort of pleasure from watching his students struggle to understand his material and questions. Normally, I shrug off these kinds of reviews and think I can get through no problem. The issue is that hard work/smarts do not equal success in this class. Success is determined by your capability to read his mind.

Worst professor I have ever had. Does not teach; only gives out hw, then proceeds to go over the hw for the whole next class. Tells you hw questions are a recipe for success, then asks never-before-seen questions on exam. 10% quiz on the 2nd day of class, essentially testing what we are going to learn during semester. Make it make sense. wishmeluck

Mean attitude towards students, always puts you down, grades extremely strict and caps your final grade at a 90. Springs random pop quizzes despite attendance not being mandatory. Exams are so unclear in instruction. Extremely disorganized man. Always yaps about whatever he wants instead of teaching.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: 0/10, grading is tough with no wiggle room and tests are only doable if you can guess what he's asking for.
Not much to say, very tough grader, exams are nothing like homework, pop quiz with not mandatory attendance, and your final is capped at a 90%. Have fun.
Pretty sure the tenure hit so now he just does not care anymore.
Some teachers get a 1 because that's what they deserve, Ed gets a 1 because that's as low as it goes, if negative numbers were here this would be very different.

Here's a philosophical question, is a teacher who doesn't teach still considered a teacher? Ed proves that they are. No teaching, hard grading, rants about his life, homework that has nothing to do with exams.

This class with Ed specifically, feels like when you get scared of an exam that is only one question, take home, and open note, because you know no one can help you. Content is easy, reading his mind is not. No one would pass without the 20 point curve on your total grade, but don't think that'll be enough.
I saw the 341 reviews saying he was great, focus on the 629 reviews, even after 4 years of undergrad and finishing my first year of grad, never have I ever had such a infuriating teacher.

Ed, if you ever come across this message, take feedback from your students. Instead of trying to make others feel bad, spend a day asking people why they struggle with your class and maybe this wouldn't be a 1/10.

I waited till he put our grades in before writing this because I was worried he would see it and be so small that he would punish us by upping the curve. That should tell you enough about this professor.
The other reviews here tell everything there is. I have nothing to add. But for your sake believe what everyone here is saying.
Couldn't finish the class, not because the content is bad or difficult but the professor is something else. He berates and belittles his students and is not looking out for them.

This is a great class for anyone who wants to hear ramblings of someone trying to relive their glory days at a beer company. No teaching will get done, only redeemable thing is that a 75 counts as an A.
No words could describe how infuriating this class is. No wonder they removed his class for some of the high impact programs at Mays. 0/10.
reviews.ratingTags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: He straight up does not teach. Exams are impossible because they have nothing to do with the homework (which is the only thing he gives you to study with). No internal consistency in grading either. Class is horribly structured and he does some ridiculous things with capping grades at max 90%.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Desnt teach during classes, goes over homework and you have to teach yourself. Attendance is not mandatory but he springs a 2.5% of total grade pop quiz randomly. Your final grade can only be max 90% because "he gives you the numbers". His exams are not grading knowledge, they grade if you can read his mind since the questions are so vague.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: 0/10 if I could.

Good luck following along in lectures. If it were not for a curve, everyone would fail this class. Nice guy, but simply cannot teach. Astounds me that he is teaching at the graduate level; I learned more in my intro to finance course in undergraduate than I did in this class. Very difficult to get an A unless you beat the curve on exams.

Prof. White is a chill guy and it is clear that he has extensive finance knowledge and experience. However, as a teacher he is awful. Talks in circles about nothing for most of class. Contradicts himself constantly. TopHat questions are not reflective of the material on the exams. Also, get ready to be confused about rounding errors.

This class was frustrating to the extreme. Prof White would contradict himself consistently and the power point formulas would not match what was taught in class. I believe he has extensive knowledge about the finance world but struggles to convey it in an understandable way. He wants his students to succeed. Exams differ from homework.

Be prepared for a surprise test in the first week, lectures that go in circles, and staying up all night to learn the homework given. Curved tests are the savior for everyone. My GA wasn't helpful but this will vary so don't take that into consideration. Weird part is he's a normal guy outside of class. Definitely take with another professor!

Ed is one of the best professors I've had. He was asked to teach the remaining portion of 341 for Summer and he was amazing. He taught the course so you could understand and get good grades. I didn't need a tutor and did fine. While I didn't get an A, I did score high compared to others (I would've had an A if it wasn't for stuff outside of class).

Best professor I have had at TAMU. He stepped in to teach FINC 341 (a naturally difficult course), and made the material understandable. I was paying for a tutor daily before he took over. His lectures were helpful enough to no longer need tutoring. Genuine man who cares about your well being and academics. Can't say enough good things

Prof. White is a great professor. You enjoy learning about bonds/stocks/NPV? Youll love this class. Not an easy A but not a class youll have to stay up studying for. If you have a finc/acct background youll be fine. Not a read notes/PowerPoint and get an A class but rather what youll see in the real world. Got B bc I woke up late for an exam :/
reviews.ratingTags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Great professor with great knowledge of the industry and really funny. The CFP Capstone class is based in case studies that are done every week and then presented on mondays. This was a great class and really helped with presentations and with critical thinking.
This class is pretty easy, Ed cares about learning and gives real life examples to his lectures. He is accessible and cares for his students.

There are lots of exams, and most of them do not look anything like the material covered in class. He gives little instruction on exam questions, so if you can't read his mind you will fail his exams. If you try to ask him for help he just talks down at you and avoids your questions. But he does curve the class at the end of the semester.

He came across very unprofessional when I went to him for help. Insteaed of helping me he told he I will not be successful in the future. Do not expect to learn anything from his class because he does not teach. Instead, he waste the majority of the class time talking about topics not related to the course.
